tools.name: dbx_execute_batch
tools.description: Execute a SQL script containing multiple statements in one call and return a result per statement. Statements are split with a database-dialect-aware parser, so semicolons inside strings, comments and stored procedures are handled. Stops at the first failing statement unless continue_on_error is true. Pass session_id (from dbx_open_session) when statements must share one connection (e.g. temporary tables, USE/SET). Pass cell_char_offset/cell_char_limit to expand long string cells in every statement's result, exactly like dbx_execute_query. When use_transaction is true and the script has multiple statements, the whole script runs in one transaction and the call returns a single merged result instead of one result per statement (single-statement scripts run normally and return that one result); use_transaction cannot be combined with session_id or continue_on_error, and is rejected when the backend cannot provide a rollbackable transaction or for MySQL-family DDL scripts (DDL implicitly commits and cannot be rolled back).

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

cell_char_offset.description: Start character offset for every string cell (default 0, max 1000000). Use the next offset reported by a truncated result to slide through a long value; narrow the query to the target row and column first.

cell_char_limit.description: Maximum characters returned per string cell (default 200, max 4000). Increase only for an explicit long-value expansion.

sql.description: SQL script containing one or more statements. Statements are split using the database-dialect-aware splitter, so semicolons inside strings, comments, and stored procedures are handled.

session_id.description: Session ID from dbx_open_session. When set, every statement runs on the session's pinned connection, preserving USE/SET, temporary tables and other session state across statements in the script and across calls.

continue_on_error.description: When true, execution continues after a statement error instead of stopping at the first failure. Connection-level failures always stop the batch. Default false (stop at first failure).

use_transaction.description: When true and the script has more than one statement, all statements run inside one transaction (BEGIN … COMMIT) so the whole batch succeeds or rolls back, and the call returns a single merged result. For a single-statement script the option is ignored and the statement runs as normal auto-commit. Backends that cannot provide a rollbackable transaction reject this option. Cannot be combined with session_id or continue_on_error. Rejected for MySQL-family DDL scripts because DDL implicitly commits and cannot be rolled back. Default is auto-commit for each statement.

tools.name: dbx_execute_query
tools.description: Execute a SQL query on a database connection (default 100 rows; pass max_rows to return up to 1000 rows; larger values are clamped; MongoDB shell commands and multi-statement scripts routed through the batch executor stay at 100 rows). For backwards compatibility, multi-statement scripts and stored-procedure scripts are routed through the dialect-aware batch executor.

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

session_id.description: Session ID from dbx_open_session. When set, the query runs on the session's pinned connection, preserving USE/SET and other session state across calls.

cell_char_offset.description: Start character offset for every string cell (default 0, max 1000000). Use the next offset reported by a truncated result to slide through a long value; narrow the query to the target row and column first.

cell_char_limit.description: Maximum characters returned per string cell (default 200, max 4000). Increase only for an explicit long-value expansion.

max_rows.description: Maximum rows returned for this call (default 100, max 1000; larger values are clamped). SQL connections only - MongoDB shell commands always return at most 100 rows, and multi-statement scripts routed to the batch executor return at most 100 rows per statement.

db.description: Redis logical database number. Use this argument instead of the SELECT command.

command.description: Redis command to execute, for example GET mykey or INFO

routine_type.description: Optional routine type filter: PROCEDURE or FUNCTION. Omit to list both. Unsupported databases return an empty list.

tools.name: dbx_list_tables

tools.name: dbx_open_session
tools.description: Open a stateful query session pinned to a single backend connection. Returns a session ID for dbx_execute_query: USE, SET CATALOG, session variables and temporary tables persist across calls within the session. Close with dbx_close_session when done; idle sessions expire after 30 minutes by default (configurable with DBX_SESSION_IDLE_TTL_SECS).

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

enable_transactions.description: Eagerly reserve one native MySQL connection for explicit transaction tools

tools.name: dbx_open_table
tools.description: Open a table in DBX desktop app. Requires DBX to be running.

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

tools.name: dbx_peek_messages
tools.description: Read up to 100 Kafka messages without committing consumer offsets. Defaults to the latest 20 messages. Returns JSON with base64 payloads, UTF-8 previews, metadata, incomplete (partial broker read), and outputTruncated (256 KiB message output budget). Only Kafka is supported.

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

start_position.description: Read latest messages (default), earliest messages, or from an offset

partition.description: Non-negative partition; omit to read across partitions

offset.description: Non-negative offset, required only for start_position=offset

tools.name: dbx_remove_connection
tools.description: Remove a database connection from DBX

connection_name.description: Name of the DBX connection when connection_id is not provided

tools.name: dbx_rollback_transaction
tools.description: Roll back the active transaction. Cleanup remains available after write-policy revocation.

session_id.description: Transaction-enabled session ID returned by dbx_open_session

tools.name: dbx_salesforce_apply_write
tools.description: Step 2 of 2 for a Salesforce write: execute exactly the write prepared by dbx_salesforce_prepare_write, identified by its confirm_token. The token is single-use, expires 5 minutes after it was issued, and is bound to that one statement — a changed write needs a new prepare. Call this only after the user has approved the summary they were shown. Returns the Salesforce result, or the org's own per-record error text.

confirm_token.description: The confirm_token returned by dbx_salesforce_prepare_write. Single-use, and valid only for the exact write that was summarized.

tools.name: dbx_salesforce_current_user
tools.description: Show the Salesforce identity behind a DBX connection: the connected user, their profile, whether that profile holds "Modify All Data" (which bypasses field-level security and record sharing), and the org. Read-only. Call it before preparing a write so the user knows who the change will be attributed to, and to tell a permission failure apart from a bad record Id.

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

tools.name: dbx_salesforce_prepare_write
tools.description: Step 1 of 2 for a Salesforce write: prepare an insert, update or delete of exactly ONE record. Nothing is sent to Salesforce. The call validates the request against DBX MCP policy and returns a human-readable summary plus a single-use confirm_token. Show that summary to the user and wait for their approval, then call dbx_salesforce_apply_write with the token. Salesforce has no transactions, so an applied write cannot be rolled back. Reads never need this: use dbx_execute_query with SOQL.

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

database.description: Database name. Salesforce has no databases, so omit this unless DBX MCP settings scope the connection.

op.description: Write operation: "insert", "update" or "delete". One record per call.

object.description: Salesforce object API name, e.g. "Account", "Contact" or a custom object such as "Invoice__c".

id.description: Record Id of the row to change. Required for update and delete; omit for insert, where Salesforce assigns it.

fields.description: Field API name to value map, e.g. {"Name": "Acme", "AnnualRevenue": 1200}. Required and non-empty for insert and update; omit for delete. Never include "Id".

tools.name: dbx_send_message
tools.description: Send a base64-encoded message to a Kafka, RocketMQ, or RabbitMQ topic/queue

connection_id.description: Unique ID of the DBX connection

payload_base64.description: Message payload encoded as standard base64

key.description: Optional message key used for partitioning

payload_text.description: Optional UTF-8 text preview of the payload

instructions: Use DBX connections to inspect schemas and query databases safely.
